Ios & Kampos

Our island, our favourite places

Kampos, our corner of Ios

Kampos means “the countryside”: a quiet hillside between the port and Skarkos hill, facing Chora.

From the house, Yalos beach is 5 minutes on foot and the port about fifteen. Skarkos hill and its ancient site are 15 minutes' walk away. Chora, the hilltop village, is reached by bus, by taxi or along the old cobbled path.

Here are the places we love and recommend to our guests.

The map shows the neighbourhood. We send you the exact address with your booking confirmation.

Must-sees

Chora

The white village and its alleys, the windmills on the ridge and the church of Panagia Gremiotissa at the very top. The best spot on the island for the sunset.

Skarkos

A Bronze Age settlement, one of the most important in the Cyclades, 15 minutes' walk from the house. Its finds are on display at the archaeological museum in Chora.

The Odysseas Elytis theatre

An ancient-style marble amphitheatre just behind the windmills. It hosts concerts in summer, facing the sea.

Homer's tomb

In the north of the island, above Plakotos. Legend has it that Homer died on Ios. The sea view alone is worth the trip.

Paleokastro

The ruins of a Venetian castle in the east of the island, between Agia Theodoti and Psathi, with spectacular views.

The fishing harbour

Caiques and nets on the quay, a few minutes from the house. In the morning, you can buy the fish that will end up on the plancha.

The beaches

In summer, the meltemi blows from the north. On very windy days, choose a sheltered beach in the south.

  • Sand
  • On foot
  • Family-friendly

Yalos

Our beach, 5 minutes' walk away. Long, sandy, shallow and well equipped, with tavernas and beach bars.

  • Sand
  • Bus
  • Lively

Mylopotas

The island's large bay, well equipped, with water sports and a party atmosphere. Served by frequent buses.

  • Sand
  • Sheltered from the wind
  • Car or boat

Manganari

In the south, a string of turquoise coves sheltered from the meltemi. The most beautiful on the island, many say.

  • Sand
  • Bus
  • Sunset

Koumbara

In the west, facing Sikinos. Exposed to the wind, but superb at the end of the day.

  • Sand
  • Bus
  • Tavernas

Agia Theodoti

In the north-east, at the end of a scenic road. A large, peaceful beach and tavernas right on the sand.

  • Wild
  • Car or boat
  • Water and picnic

Psathi, Kalamos, Papas, Tris Klisies

The wild beaches of the east and south-east, with no facilities at all. For a timeless day out, with a car and a picnic basket.

Our favourite places

The restaurants, bars and shops we recommend. Most of them open from May to October.

Tavernas

  • The Octopus Tree, Yalos harbour the closest to the house. Grilled octopus, meze and courgette fritters by the water.
  • Katogi, Chora meze in a lovely courtyard. Try the pasta salad with local cheese. Book a few days ahead.
  • Lord Byron, Chora a mezedopoleio with a bohemian feel, a safe bet for years.
  • Drakos, Mylopotas charcoal-grilled fish at the end of the beach, since 1963.
  • Ithaka, port more modern Mediterranean cooking, such as octopus on fava purée.

A sunset drink

  • Ios Club, Chora on the ridge above the port since 1968. Classical music and cocktails while the sun goes down.
  • Steps Bar, Chora a drink on cushion-covered steps, below the windmills.
  • Pathos, Koumbara a lounge restaurant on the hill, facing the sunset.

Local produce and groceries

  • Skotiri the cheese of Ios, fresh and tangy, matured in a goatskin bag with thyme and savory. You will find it on almost every table.
  • Diaseli cheese dairy, north of the island a family cheese dairy with a small museum and tastings.
  • Mosenta thyme honey, island cheeses, pasteli and jams.
  • The fishing harbour fresh fish in the morning, when the boats come in
  • Mini Market and Aegean Market the closest to the house, on Yalos beach and at the port

Activities

  • Boat trip around the island boats leave from Yalos harbour for the southern beaches, which you cannot reach by road.
  • Ios Adventure, Chora guided walks, as far as the Diaseli cheese dairy, and e-bike rides to Homer's tomb.
  • Diving, kayaking and paddleboarding, Mylopotas the Meltemi Dive and New Dive centres, on the beach.
  • Car or scooter hire several rental companies at the port and in Chora

Opening hours change every season: call or book before you go, especially in July and August.

On foot, by boat, at sunset

The Ios Paths project has restored waymarked trails across the island. From the house, the Yalos, Skarkos, Chora loop and back is about 4 km: it is our favourite late-afternoon walk.

For sunsets, climb up to the windmills of Chora or to the church of Panagia Gremiotissa. In summer, don't miss a village festival, the panigiri: music, dancing and a shared meal until late into the night.

Neighbouring islands in a day

Ios lies at the heart of the Cyclades. Times are for fast boats. Check the seasonal timetables before you go.

Island Crossing Why go
Sikinos 10 to 30 min The closest and most authentic, with no crowds.
Santorini 35 to 50 min The caldera and the villages of Oia and Fira.
Folegandros 40 min to 1 h 30 min One of the most beautiful Choras in the Cyclades, on the edge of a cliff.
Naxos 35 to 45 min The Portara, the mountain villages and the long beaches.
Paros about 1 h Naoussa, Parikia and their alleys. Best with a night there.
